props.title: Wild Grass
props.initialSlug: Love blooms from a lost wallet in peculiar ways

sections.content: Alain Resnais's **Wild Grass** (2009) represents a stunning late-career masterpiece that playfully deconstructs romantic obsession. Like his earlier Last Year at Marienbad (1961), it weaves reality and fantasy into an intoxicating puzzle. The film follows Georges (André Dussollier), who finds a stolen wallet belonging to Marguerite (Sabine Azéma), triggering an increasingly bizarre series of events. Resnais channels the spirit of **Vertigo** (1958) but adds his signature surrealist touch, using saturated colors and dreamlike transitions to blur the line between imagination and reality.

sections.content: The film's exploration of chance encounters echoes other French New Wave experiments like Jacques Rivette's **Céline and Julie Go Boating** (1974). Resnais, at 87 when directing **Wild Grass**, demonstrates the same innovative spirit that marked his breakthrough **Hiroshima Mon Amour** (1959). The film's yellow-tinted scenes and Eric Gautier's fluid cinematography create a heightened reality where mundane moments transform into magical possibilities.

Like fellow French director Michel Gondry's **Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind** (2004), **Wild Grass** plays with memory and desire while maintaining an offbeat sense of humor. The film's structure deliberately frustrates conventional narrative expectations, similar to how **Mulholland Drive** (2001) subverts noir tropes. Resnais crafts a meditation on cinema itself, with references to classic films and a meta-awareness of storytelling conventions. SUBHEAD: Late Period Innovation

sections.content: **Wild Grass** marks a pivotal moment in Resnais's late period, alongside **Private Fears in Public Places** (2006) and **Life of Riley** (2014). These films share a theatrical playfulness and formal experimentation that influenced directors like Leos Carax, particularly in **Holy Motors** (2012). The artificial sets and heightened performances create a distinctly cinematic universe where reality bends to emotional truth.
